operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a todo item from the todo_list_todos table. It performs a hard deletion that completely removes the record from the database. The operation validates that the todo exists and belongs to the requesting user before allowing deletion. Since the schema includes a deleted_at field for soft deletion capability, this operation provides an alternative for users who want to permanently remove items without using the soft deletion mechanism.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a todo item
operations.description:
Permanently remove a todo item from the database. This operation performs a hard deletion that completely eliminates the record, unlike soft deletion which marks items as deleted while preserving them for audit purposes.

The operation validates that the todo item exists and belongs to the authenticated user before allowing deletion. It provides users with the option to permanently remove items they no longer need, which can be useful for cleaning up completed tasks or removing erroneous entries.

Security considerations include user ownership verification and appropriate error handling for unauthorized access attempts. Since this is a permanent deletion operation, users should be aware that deleted items cannot be recovered. Related operations include soft deletion alternatives and todo retrieval operations for viewing active items.

This operation does not return any content upon successful deletion, providing a clean confirmation of the removal process.

It operates on the todo_list_todo_snapshots table from the Prisma schema and supports filtering and pagination capabilities to browse through the audit trail of todo item changes over time.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve historical snapshots of a specific todo item
operations.description:
This operation provides access to the complete audit trail and version history of a todo item by retrieving paginated snapshots. Each snapshot represents a point-in-time capture of the todo's state whenever significant changes occurred (title, description, or status modifications).

The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Users can sort snapshots by creation date to view the chronological evolution of the todo item. The system automatically creates snapshots when todo items are modified, providing an append-only record for compliance and recovery purposes.

Security considerations include ensuring that users can only access snapshots for todo items they own. The operation validates that the referenced todo exists and belongs to the authenticated user before returning snapshot data. Rate limiting applies to prevent excessive historical data queries.

This operation integrates with the todo_list_todo_snapshots table as defined in the Prisma schema, incorporating all available snapshot fields including title, description, status, and creation timestamp. The response includes snapshot summary information optimized for historical browsing.

operations.summary: Retrieve detailed information for a specific todo snapshot
operations.description:
This operation provides access to a specific historical snapshot of a todo item, returning the complete state information that was captured at the time of snapshot creation. Each snapshot preserves the title, description, and status of the todo item at a specific moment, enabling detailed historical analysis and audit trail verification.

The operation validates that both the todo item and snapshot exist and belong to the authenticated user before returning the detailed snapshot data. Security measures ensure that users can only access snapshots for todo items they own, maintaining proper data isolation between users.

This operation is particularly useful for compliance auditing, version comparison, and recovery scenarios where users need to examine specific historical states of their todo items. The snapshot data provides a complete record of what the todo item contained at the time of capture, including any descriptions and status information.

This operation integrates with the todo_list_todo_snapshots table as defined in the Prisma schema, returning all available snapshot fields with their historical values. The response includes the complete snapshot data for detailed examination.

can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:

refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

id.description: Primary key identifier for the user account. Generated automatically when the user record is created using UUID v4 format for global uniqueness.

status.description: Current user account status. Valid values: active, inactive, suspended. Controls login capability and system access. Active status allows full system functionality, inactive restricts access to read-only operations, and suspended blocks all system interactions pending administrative review.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was created. Automatically set when the user record is first saved to the database using the system's current UTC time.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated. Automatically updated whenever the user record is modified, tracking the most recent changes to user profile information.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was soft deleted. Null indicates active account. Used for audit purposes and data retention compliance, allowing account restoration within configured retention periods.

ITodoListUser.description:
Complete user account entity representing authenticated users in the todo list application.

Stores user credentials, profile information, and account management data for secure access to the todo management system. Each user account enables creation, management, and organization of personal todo items with complete data isolation from other users.

The model includes comprehensive authentication fields for secure login functionality and supports detailed account status tracking for administrative management. User data is protected with industry-standard encryption practices and follows privacy requirements specified in the security documentation.

Used throughout the application for user authentication, profile management, access control, and administrative oversight. The entity maintains referential integrity with todo items and user sessions through proper database relationships.

email.description:
User's email address for account registration and authentication.

Must be a valid email address following RFC 5322 standards and unique across all user accounts in the system. The email serves as the primary identifier for user authentication and communication.

During registration, the system validates email format and checks for uniqueness to prevent duplicate account creation. Email addresses are stored in lowercase format for consistency.

password.description:
Plain text password provided by the user during registration.

This password will be securely hashed using bcrypt with appropriate salt rounds before being stored in the password_hash field of the todo_list_users table.

The system enforces password strength requirements including minimum length, character diversity, and common password prevention to ensure account security.

ITodoListUser.ICreate.description:
Data transfer object for creating new user accounts in the todo list application.

Used exclusively during the user registration process to collect essential account creation information. This DTO contains only the fields that users can provide during registration - email and password.

The system automatically manages all other user account properties including status (set to 'active'), timestamps (created_at, updated_at), and soft deletion tracking (deleted_at). Password hashing and email validation are performed server-side to ensure security and data integrity.

This schema represents the minimal information required to establish a new user identity while maintaining security best practices and preventing unnecessary data exposure during the registration workflow.

email.description:
User's registered email address used for authentication.

Must match exactly the email address stored in the todo_list_users table, including case sensitivity. The system performs a lookup by email to retrieve the corresponding user record for password verification.

Email validation ensures the account exists and is in an active status before proceeding with password comparison.

password.description:
User's plain text password for authentication verification.

This password is compared against the stored password_hash in the todo_list_users table using bcrypt verification. The system performs secure password comparison without exposing timing information that could be used for credential enumeration attacks.

Successful authentication requires matching credentials and an active account status in the system.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring.

Captures the network source of the login request for audit trail purposes. This information is used to create session records in the todo_list_user_sessions table for security monitoring and user activity tracking.

The IP address helps identify suspicious login patterns and provides context for security incident investigation. Optional field - server can extract from request if not provided.

href.description:
Connection URL where the login request originated.

Provides the specific endpoint or page that initiated the authentication request. This field is required for session context establishment and helps track user navigation patterns through the application.

The href value ensures proper session management and supports audit trail requirements for compliance and security monitoring.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that directed the user to the login page.

Indicates the previous page or external source that led the user to the authentication endpoint. This information is valuable for understanding user journeys and detecting potential phishing attempts or unauthorized access patterns.

Referrer tracking supports security analysis and user experience optimization by providing context for authentication flow entry points.

ITodoListUser.ILogin.description:
User authentication credentials and session context for secure login operations.

This schema represents the complete authentication request containing both user credentials (email and password) and session metadata (ip, href, referrer) for comprehensive security tracking.

The primary authentication fields (email and password) are validated against the todo_list_users table records using bcrypt password verification. The session context fields are used to create detailed session records in the todo_list_user_sessions table for security monitoring and audit compliance.

While credentials are essential for authentication, session context fields provide valuable security information for tracking login sources, detecting suspicious patterns, and maintaining compliance with security requirements. The operation ensures proper separation between authentication validation and session context recording to maintain system security and user privacy.

refresh_token.description: Valid refresh token obtained from previous authentication session. This token is used to issue new access tokens without requiring full re-authentication. The token must be valid, unexpired, and not revoked to successfully extend the user session.

ITodoListUser.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token request for extending user authentication sessions without requiring full re-login.

This schema contains the single refresh token parameter required to obtain new authentication tokens. The operation validates the provided refresh token against the authentication system's token store, ensuring it hasn't been revoked or expired before issuing new access and refresh tokens.

The refresh mechanism follows OAuth 2.0 best practices for token management, providing continuous access to todo management features while maintaining security through periodic token rotation. This operation is essential for mobile applications and web interfaces where users expect persistent sessions without frequent re-authentication requirements.

Successful token refresh returns a complete ITodoListUser.IAuthorized response with updated tokens and user information, enabling seamless continuation of todo management activities while maintaining strong security controls.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated user from the todo_list_users table. Generated automatically using UUID v4 format upon user registration. This ID serves as the primary key for all user-related operations and ensures data isolation between different user accounts.

email.description: User's email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all users and validated against RFC 5322 email format standards. This email serves as the primary identifier for user accounts and is used for password reset functionality and system notifications.

status.description: Current user account status. Valid values: active, inactive, suspended. Controls login capability and system access. Active status allows full system functionality, inactive restricts access to read-only operations, and suspended blocks all system interactions pending administrative review.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was created. Automatically set when the user record is first saved to the database using the system's current UTC time.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated. Automatically updated whenever the user record is modified, tracking the most recent changes to user profile information.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was soft deleted. Null indicates active account. Used for audit purposes and data retention compliance, allowing account restoration within configured retention periods.

ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.description:
Authentication response containing user identity and access tokens for secure API interaction.

This schema represents the successful authentication response returned after user registration, login, or token refresh operations. It provides the authenticated user's essential identity information along with JWT tokens necessary for accessing protected todo management endpoints.

The response includes only the essential user identity fields (id and email) and authentication tokens. All security-sensitive fields like password_hash and system-managed fields like status, timestamps, and deletion tracking are excluded to prevent data exposure and maintain security best practices.

This secure response enables seamless user experience by providing immediate access to todo management features while maintaining strong security controls through proper data protection and token management.

ITodoListUserSession.description:
User authentication session entity for tracking login activity and security context.

Records user login sessions with connection details including IP address, URL, and referrer information. Each session represents an authenticated connection from a specific device and location.

Sessions are used for audit tracing of user actions and support multi-device access with proper security monitoring. The model follows the exact session table pattern with required fields for security compliance.

id.description:
Primary key identifier for the configuration entry. Automatically generated by the system when the configuration is created.

This UUID serves as the unique identifier for each configuration record in the database. It is immutable and cannot be modified after creation. The ID is used internally for database operations and relationships.

key.description:
Unique configuration key identifier used to reference specific settings throughout the application. Must be unique across all configuration entries.

Configuration keys follow a hierarchical naming convention (e.g., 'ui.theme.dark', 'performance.cache.ttl') to organize related settings. Keys are case-sensitive and should use lowercase letters with dots for hierarchy separation. This field is required and cannot be null.

value.description:
Configuration value stored as string. Can represent various data types (boolean, number, text) that are parsed by the application logic.

The value field stores the actual configuration setting that controls application behavior. Common formats include: 'true'/'false' for booleans, numeric strings for numbers, and free text for descriptive settings. The application parses these values based on the expected data type for each configuration key.

description.description:
Human-readable description explaining the purpose and usage of this configuration setting. Helps administrators understand what the setting controls.

Descriptions should clearly explain the configuration's function, valid values, and impact on the application. For example: 'Controls whether dark theme is enabled system-wide. Accepts true/false values.' This field is optional but recommended for better configuration management.

category.description:
Optional category grouping for organizing related configurations. Examples: 'ui', 'performance', 'security', 'features'.

Categories help organize configurations into logical groups for easier management and browsing. Common categories include user interface settings, performance tuning parameters, security configurations, and feature flags. This field is optional and can be null if no category is assigned.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this configuration was initially created. Tracks when settings were first established in the system.

This field is automatically set by the database when the configuration record is created. It cannot be modified and provides audit capability for tracking when specific configurations were introduced to the system.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this configuration was last modified. Used for tracking configuration changes and version control.

The system automatically updates this timestamp whenever any field in the configuration is modified. This provides version control capability and helps identify when configuration changes occurred.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when this configuration was soft-deleted. Allows configurations to be disabled without permanent removal, supporting audit trails and recovery capabilities.

When a configuration is no longer needed, it can be soft-deleted by setting this timestamp. Soft-deleted configurations are typically excluded from normal application usage but remain in the database for historical and recovery purposes. This field is null for active configurations.

ITodoListConfiguration.description:
System-level configuration settings for the Todo List application.

This entity represents key-value pairs that control application behavior, feature flags, and system parameters. Configurations are managed at the system level and affect the entire application rather than individual users.

Each configuration entry consists of a unique key identifier and a corresponding value that can represent various data types. The system supports categorization for better organization and includes descriptive information to help administrators understand each setting's purpose.

Configuration records include audit timestamps for tracking creation, modification, and deletion. Soft deletion is supported to maintain historical records while allowing configurations to be disabled without permanent removal.

key.description:
Unique configuration key identifier used to reference specific settings throughout the application. Must be unique across all configuration entries.

Configuration keys follow a hierarchical naming convention (e.g., 'ui.theme.dark', 'performance.cache.ttl') to organize related settings. Keys are case-sensitive and should use lowercase letters with dots for hierarchy separation. This field is required for configuration creation.

value.description:
Configuration value stored as string. Can represent various data types (boolean, number, text) that are parsed by the application logic.

The value field stores the actual configuration setting that controls application behavior. Common formats include: 'true'/'false' for booleans, numeric strings for numbers, and free text for descriptive settings. The application parses these values based on the expected data type for each configuration key.

description.description:
Human-readable description explaining the purpose and usage of this configuration setting. Helps administrators understand what the setting controls.

Descriptions should clearly explain the configuration's function, valid values, and impact on the application. For example: 'Controls whether dark theme is enabled system-wide. Accepts true/false values.' This field is optional but recommended for better configuration management.

category.description:
Optional category grouping for organizing related configurations. Examples: 'ui', 'performance', 'security', 'features'.

Categories help organize configurations into logical groups for easier management and browsing. Common categories include user interface settings, performance tuning parameters, security configurations, and feature flags. This field is optional and can be null if no category is assigned.

ITodoListConfiguration.ICreate.description:
Data required to create a new system-level configuration setting.

This DTO contains the essential information needed to establish a new configuration entry in the Todo List application. It includes the configuration key, value, and optional descriptive information for better management.

When creating a configuration, the system automatically generates the ID, created_at, and updated_at fields. The deleted_at field remains null until the configuration is soft-deleted. The key must be unique across all existing configuration entries.

value.description:
Updated configuration value stored as string. Can represent various data types (boolean, number, text) that are parsed by the application logic.

If provided, this value will replace the existing configuration value. Common formats include: 'true'/'false' for booleans, numeric strings for numbers, and free text for descriptive settings. The application parses these values based on the expected data type for each configuration key.

description.description:
Updated human-readable description explaining the purpose and usage of this configuration setting.

If provided, this description will replace the existing configuration description. Descriptions should clearly explain the configuration's function, valid values, and impact on the application.

category.description:
Updated category grouping for organizing related configurations. Examples: 'ui', 'performance', 'security', 'features'.

If provided, this category will replace the existing configuration category. Categories help organize configurations into logical groups for easier management and browsing.

ITodoListConfiguration.IUpdate.description:
Data required to update an existing system-level configuration setting.

This DTO supports partial updates, meaning only the fields provided will be modified while other fields remain unchanged. This allows for flexible configuration management without requiring complete re-specification of all configuration properties.

When updating a configuration, the system automatically refreshes the updated_at timestamp to track when the modification occurred. The configuration key and ID cannot be modified as they serve as immutable identifiers.

key.description: Unique configuration key identifier used to reference specific settings throughout the application. Must be unique across all configuration entries and follows naming conventions for system parameters. Used for programmatic access to configuration values.

value.description: Configuration value stored as string representation. Can represent various data types including boolean flags, numeric values, text content, or JSON structures that are parsed by the application logic. Values are validated according to configuration type requirements.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this configuration was last modified. Used for tracking configuration changes, version control, and identifying recent updates to system settings.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when this configuration was soft-deleted. Allows configurations to be disabled without permanent removal, supporting audit trails and recovery capabilities while maintaining historical records.

ITodoListConfiguration.ISummary.description:
Summary view of system-level configuration settings for the Todo List application.

Provides a lightweight representation of configuration entries suitable for list views, administrative interfaces, and quick reference scenarios. Includes essential fields needed for configuration identification, basic usage, and lifecycle tracking.

This summary variant maintains the core functionality of configuration management while optimizing for performance in scenarios where complete configuration details are not required. The inclusion of timestamp fields supports audit trail capabilities and configuration lifecycle management.

Used primarily in configuration listing operations, search results, and administrative interfaces where quick access to configuration metadata is needed without fetching full configuration details.

key.description: Filter configurations by key pattern or exact match. Supports partial matching for finding configurations with similar naming patterns. Useful for locating related configuration groups or specific settings by name.

category.description: Filter configurations by category grouping. Allows administrators to focus on specific configuration types such as UI settings, performance parameters, security controls, or feature flags. Supports category-based organization and management.

include_deleted.description: Whether to include soft-deleted configurations in search results. When true, returns both active and deleted configurations for comprehensive audit and recovery purposes. When false, only returns active configurations.

created_at.description: Filter configurations by creation date range. Useful for finding configurations created during specific time periods or for audit trail analysis. Supports date-based filtering for configuration lifecycle management.

updated_at.description: Filter configurations by last modification date. Helps identify recently changed settings or configurations modified during specific maintenance windows. Supports tracking of configuration changes over time.

deleted_at.description: Filter configurations by deletion date. Useful for audit purposes and recovery operations to identify when configurations were soft-deleted and potentially restore them if needed.

ITodoListConfiguration.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering parameters for configuration management operations in the Todo List application.

Provides comprehensive filtering capabilities for locating configuration entries based on multiple criteria including key patterns, category groupings, creation dates, modification dates, and deletion status. Supports advanced search scenarios for configuration administration and audit purposes.

All parameters are optional, allowing flexible querying from simple key-based searches to complex multi-criteria filtering. The filtering system supports both exact matches and pattern-based searches for efficient configuration management.

Used primarily in configuration listing operations where administrators need to locate specific settings, analyze configuration patterns, or perform audit trail reviews. The flexible filtering approach accommodates various administrative workflows and reporting requirements.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Starts from 1 for the first page of results. Used to navigate through large datasets efficiently.

limit.description: Number of user records to return per page. Maximum limit of 100 records per request to maintain system performance and prevent resource exhaustion.

search.description: Search term to filter users by email address. Supports partial matching and case-insensitive search functionality for flexible user discovery.

oneOf.description: Filter users by specific account status. Valid values: active (fully operational), inactive (temporarily disabled), suspended (administratively blocked). If not provided, returns users of all statuses.

status.description: Filter users by specific account status. Valid values: active (fully operational), inactive (temporarily disabled), suspended (administratively blocked). If not provided, returns users of all statuses.

order.description: Sorting direction for the results. Ascending (asc) orders from smallest to largest, descending (desc) orders from largest to smallest.

ITodoListUser.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering parameters for retrieving paginated lists of todo list users.

This request DTO provides comprehensive search capabilities for finding users based on multiple criteria including email patterns, account status, and registration date ranges. It supports robust pagination functionality with configurable page sizes and sorting options.

The search parameter supports partial matching on email addresses, enabling users to find accounts without knowing the complete email. Status filtering allows administrators to view users based on their current account state (active, inactive, or suspended).

Pagination parameters ensure efficient browsing of large user datasets while maintaining system performance. The operation respects privacy requirements by filtering sensitive information based on the requesting user's authorization level.

Used in user search operations to provide flexible filtering and sorting capabilities for administrative interfaces and user management workflows.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description:
Data transfer object for updating existing user accounts with partial modification capabilities.

Allows modification of user profile information and account status while maintaining security constraints. All fields are optional to support partial updates where only specific attributes need modification.

Password changes are handled through dedicated authentication endpoints rather than general user updates for security reasons. System-generated timestamps (created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are managed automatically by the database and cannot be modified through this DTO.

Used in user profile updates and administrative account management operations where selective field modification is required without affecting authentication credentials or system-managed metadata.

ITodoListUserSession.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of user sessions for administrative views and audit logs.

Contains essential session information for display in lists and monitoring interfaces. Focuses on identification, user context, connection details, and timing information while excluding full authentication context.

This summary includes connection metadata such as IP address, URL, and referrer for comprehensive security auditing. The user reference provides context without exposing sensitive account information.

Used for session management, security monitoring, user activity tracking, and compliance auditing throughout the application. Supports multi-device access tracking and security incident investigation.

page.description:
Page number for paginated session retrieval. Starts from 1 for the first page. Used in conjunction with limit parameter to control pagination behavior.

This parameter enables efficient handling of large session datasets by breaking results into manageable pages. The system automatically calculates the offset based on page number and limit value.

limit.description:
Maximum number of sessions to return per page. The system enforces a maximum limit of 100 sessions per request for performance optimization.

Smaller limit values improve response times for large session datasets, while larger values reduce the number of API calls needed to retrieve complete session histories.

ip.description:
Filter sessions by IP address using partial matching. Supports searching for specific IP addresses or IP ranges.

This filter enables security investigations by allowing users to search for sessions originating from specific locations or networks. The system performs case-insensitive partial matching on IP addresses.

created_at_start.description:

This parameter enables users to search for sessions created after a specific date, useful for investigating security incidents within specific timeframes.

created_at_end.description:
End date and time for filtering sessions by creation timestamp. Uses ISO 8601 format and works in conjunction with created_at_start.

When combined with created_at_start, this parameter creates a date range filter for session creation times, enabling precise temporal searches.

expired.description:
Filter sessions by expiration status. Set to true to retrieve only expired sessions, false for active sessions, or omit to include both.

This filter helps users distinguish between currently active sessions and historical session records for security monitoring and cleanup purposes.

oneOf.description: Sort sessions by creation timestamp. Most recent sessions appear first when combined with descending order.

order_by.description:

oneOf.description: Sort results in ascending order (oldest first for dates, A-Z for text).

order.description:

ITodoListUserSession.IRequest.description:

Security considerations include proper authorization checks to ensure users can only access their own session information. The filtering capabilities enable users to perform detailed security analysis while maintaining data privacy and access control boundaries.

ip.description:
IP address of the client connection where the session is being established. Used for security monitoring, geographic tracking, and incident investigation.

This field records the originating IP address for each authentication session, providing crucial information for security audits and suspicious activity detection across different locations. The server can extract this from request headers, but clients may provide it explicitly for SSR scenarios.

href.description:

referrer.description:

ITodoListUserSession.ICreate.description:

The session creation process establishes a secure connection between the user account and the authentication context, recording geographical, temporal, and navigational information for comprehensive security monitoring. ip.description: IP address of the connection where the session was established. Used for security auditing and geographic tracking of user access patterns. Captures the network location of the user's device during authentication.

href.description: URL of the connection where the session was created. Records the specific page or endpoint that initiated the session establishment. Useful for tracking user entry points and application navigation patterns.

referrer.description: Referrer URL that directed the user to the application. Useful for tracking user navigation paths and marketing campaign effectiveness. May be empty for direct access or bookmarked URLs.

ITodoListUserSessions.description:
Secure response DTO for user authentication sessions containing only connection metadata for security auditing purposes.

This schema represents a security-hardened view of user sessions that excludes authentication context and system-generated fields. Only connection metadata (IP address, URL, referrer) is exposed to prevent security breaches through authentication context exposure.

The schema follows zero-trust security principles by removing all user identity information (todo_list_user_id) and system-generated fields (id, timestamps). This prevents authentication bypass vulnerabilities and ensures clients cannot manipulate server-managed data.

Connection metadata is retained for legitimate security auditing purposes while maintaining user privacy and system integrity. This approach balances security requirements with necessary audit trail capabilities.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the todo item was last modified. Updated automatically whenever any field changes, providing audit trail for modifications. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format for interoperability.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the todo item was soft deleted. Null indicates an active item that hasn't been deleted. Supports soft deletion functionality while preserving historical records for audit purposes.

ITodoListTodo.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering parameters for retrieving paginated todo items with advanced query capabilities.

This request schema defines comprehensive search criteria available for todo item retrieval operations. It supports multiple filtering dimensions including text search, status filtering, customizable sorting options, and user ownership filtering.

The schema enforces reasonable limits on result sizes and provides flexible ordering capabilities to meet various user interface requirements. All parameters are designed to work efficiently with the database indexes defined in the todo_list_todos table for optimal performance.

Security considerations ensure that user filtering provides proper authorization and data isolation between users. The schema supports complex query scenarios while maintaining simplicity for common use cases through sensible defaults and optional parameters.

title.description:
Required todo item title that identifies the task. Must be between 1-255 characters as specified in business requirements. The title serves as the primary identifier for the todo item and is displayed in lists and interfaces.

Business rules require that every todo must have a title to ensure meaningful task identification. The character limit prevents excessively long titles while allowing sufficient description for most use cases.

description.description:
Optional detailed description providing additional context for the todo item. Can contain up to 1000 characters of explanatory text, notes, or supplementary information.

This field supports rich task documentation while maintaining reasonable storage limits. When omitted, the todo relies solely on the title for task identification. Useful for complex tasks requiring detailed instructions or background information.

oneOf.description: Initial status indicating the todo item is awaiting completion. This is the default state for newly created todos and represents tasks that have not yet been started or completed.
Initial status indicating the todo item has been finished. Allows creating todos in completed state for tasks that were accomplished before system tracking began.

status.description:
Initial status setting for the todo item upon creation. Valid values are 'pending' (default) or 'completed'.

Status transitions follow business workflow rules where todos typically start as 'pending' and progress to 'completed'. The system allows setting completed status during creation for retrospective task tracking or pre-completed items.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description:
Data transfer object for creating new todo items in the todo management system.

Contains only user-provided fields required for todo creation, excluding system-managed fields like id, timestamps, and user ownership which are automatically handled by the backend. The DTO enforces business rules including title length constraints and valid status transitions.

Used in todo creation operations where authenticated users submit new task information. The system automatically assigns ownership to the authenticated user, sets creation timestamps, and validates input against business constraints before persisting the new todo item.

Security considerations ensure proper user authentication and ownership assignment. Validation rules prevent invalid data from entering the system while providing clear error messages for constraint violations.

ITodoListTodo.IUpdate.description:
Data transfer object for updating existing todo items with partial modification data.

Supports flexible task management by allowing updates to individual fields without requiring complete todo information. All fields are optional to enable targeted modifications such as marking completion, refining descriptions, or correcting titles.

The DTO excludes immutable system-managed fields like id and creation timestamps, focusing only on user-modifiable content. Business rules ensure valid status transitions and respect field length constraints during updates.

Used in todo modification operations where authenticated users update their own tasks. The system validates ownership, applies changes to mutable fields only, and automatically updates the modification timestamp to track edit history.

Security measures verify user ownership before allowing modifications, preventing unauthorized access to other users' todo items. Error handling provides clear feedback for validation failures and ownership conflicts.

title.description:
Updated title for the todo item. Must meet the same 1-255 character constraints as creation. Allows users to refine or correct task descriptions after initial creation.

Useful for clarifying ambiguous titles or updating task focus as requirements evolve. The system validates the updated title against business rules before applying changes.

description.description:
Updated detailed description for the todo item. Supports adding, modifying, or removing supplementary task information up to 1000 characters.

Enables users to enhance task documentation, add new instructions, or provide additional context as work progresses. Optional field that can be set to null to remove existing descriptions.

oneOf.description: Status value indicating the todo item should be marked as awaiting completion. Useful for reopening completed tasks or correcting status errors.
Status value indicating the todo item should be marked as finished. Represents the completion of work described in the todo item.

status.description:
Updated status for the todo item. Supports status transitions between 'pending' and 'completed' states according to business workflow rules.

The system tracks status changes for progress monitoring and reporting. Status updates typically represent task completion milestones or workflow adjustments.

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo snapshot record. Generated automatically using UUID v4 format when the snapshot is created. This identifier provides the primary key for accessing specific historical states of todo items.

title.description: The exact title of the todo item at the moment the snapshot was captured. This field preserves the todo's title as it existed when significant changes triggered snapshot creation, enabling accurate historical tracking of title modifications over time.

description.description: Detailed description content of the todo item at the time of snapshot creation. This field captures the complete description state, including any formatting or content that was present when the snapshot was taken. The description is optional as some todo items may not have detailed descriptions.

status.description: The operational status of the todo item when the snapshot was created. This field preserves the exact status value (e.g., 'pending', 'in-progress', 'completed') that was active at the snapshot moment, providing crucial context for understanding the todo's workflow state historically.

created_at.description: Precise timestamp indicating when this snapshot was automatically generated. Uses ISO 8601 format to ensure consistent datetime representation across systems. This timestamp is critical for establishing the chronological order of snapshots and understanding the evolution of todo item states over time.

ITodoListTodoSnapshot.description:
Historical snapshots of todo items for audit trail and version tracking.

Captures point-in-time states of todo items whenever significant changes occur (title, description, or status changes). Each snapshot preserves the complete state of a todo item at a specific moment, enabling historical tracking and audit capabilities. Snapshots serve as immutable records that cannot be modified once created, ensuring data integrity for compliance and recovery purposes.

These snapshots are automatically generated by the system whenever a todo item undergoes meaningful modification. The snapshot mechanism provides an append-only audit trail that allows users to review the complete history of their todo items, including what changes were made and when they occurred. This functionality is essential for compliance auditing, version comparison, and recovery scenarios.

The snapshot entity maintains relationships with the original todo item through foreign key references, ensuring that each snapshot can be traced back to its source todo. This design supports efficient querying and retrieval of historical data while maintaining proper data isolation between different users' todo items.

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo snapshot record. Provides the primary key for snapshot identification and retrieval operations. This UUID ensures each snapshot can be uniquely referenced in list views and summary displays.

title.description: The title of the todo item as captured in the snapshot. This field provides the essential identifying information needed for quick recognition of snapshot content in list views, enabling users to quickly identify which historical state they wish to examine.

status.description: The status of the todo item at the time the snapshot was created. This field provides crucial context about the todo's workflow state historically, helping users understand the progression of their todo items through different status stages over time.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the snapshot was created. This field is essential for establishing chronological order and understanding the timing of historical changes to todo items. The datetime format ensures consistent sorting and filtering capabilities in list displays.

ITodoListTodoSnapshot.ISummary.description:
Summary view of todo item snapshots optimized for list displays.

Provides essential information for displaying historical todo states in lists and overview screens. This variant includes only the most critical fields needed for quick identification of snapshot content and timing, specifically designed to reduce payload size and improve performance in list contexts.

The summary intentionally excludes the detailed description field to optimize for list performance while maintaining the core identity and status information required for effective audit trail management. This design decision balances information density with performance considerations, ensuring that list operations remain fast and responsive even when dealing with large numbers of historical snapshots.

This summary view is particularly useful for browsing snapshot histories, conducting quick audits, and selecting specific historical states for detailed examination. The focused field selection enables efficient rendering of snapshot lists while preserving the essential information needed for meaningful historical analysis and decision-making.

ITodoListTodoSnapshot.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for snapshot filtering.

This DTO supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options for browsing historical snapshots of todo items. Users can sort snapshots by creation date to view the chronological evolution of the todo item.

The operation validates that the referenced todo exists and belongs to the authenticated user before returning snapshot data. Rate limiting applies to prevent excessive historical data queries.

This request DTO integrates with the todo_list_todo_snapshots table as defined in the Prisma schema, supporting efficient filtering and pagination of audit trail data.

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-based). Defaults to 1 if not specified.

limit.description: Number of items per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Defaults to 20.

sort_by.description: Field to sort results by. Currently supports 'created_at' for chronological ordering.

oneOf.description: Sorting direction. 'asc' for ascending (oldest first), 'desc' for descending (newest first). Defaults to 'desc'.
Sorting direction. 'asc' for ascending (oldest first), 'desc' for descending (newest first). Defaults to 'desc'.
